items.title: Switch TLS implementation from OpenSSL to rustls
items.subtitle: Adopting pure Rust TLS to eliminate OpenSSL CVE surface
items.narrative: The TLS implementation choice was revised from OpenSSL to rustls. OpenSSL is a mature but historically CVE-prone C library. Rustls provides equivalent TLS functionality written entirely in safe Rust, removing the attack surface from memory-safety vulnerabilities that plague C-based TLS libraries. This is a security-first architectural decision to reduce operational risk and attack surface in production deployments.
items.facts: ["Previous TLS selection: OpenSSL (C library)","New TLS selection: rustls (pure Rust implementation)","Motivation: Eliminate CVE vulnerabilities inherent to OpenSSL","rustls eliminates unsafe C code dependencies"]

items.title: LRU cache with 300-second TTL selected for simplicity
items.subtitle: Chose LRU over alternatives for improved maintainability and reasoning clarity.
items.narrative: The caching strategy decision prioritizes simplicity and maintainability. Rather than a more complex caching mechanism, LRU with a fixed 300-second TTL was selected because it provides a straightforward model that is easier for developers to understand, predict, and debug. This trades potential optimization complexity for clarity and operational ease.
